title: Evaluation-preserving scalar comparison respects its double transpose
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, let $A\to B$ be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and use the ordinary unbounded module derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $S=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $H_R(U,V)=R\mathcal Hom_R(U,V)$ for $R=A,B$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Use the canonical tensor comparisons of ringed-topos derived pullback [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], with the signed symmetry $\tau$ of complexes. Choose $\Omega_A\in D(A)$, $\Omega_B\in D(B)$ and a morphism $u:S\Omega_A\to\Omega_B$. Put $D_R T=H_R(T,\Omega_R)$, let $\operatorname{ev}^R_T:D_RT\otimes_R^LT\to\Omega_R$ be evaluation, and define $\delta^R_T:T\to D_R^2T$ as the tensor-Hom transpose of $\operatorname{ev}^R_T\circ\tau_{T,D_RT}$.

Let $K\in D(A)$ and suppose, for $T=K$ and $T=D_AK$, that maps $h_T:S(D_AT)\to D_B(ST)$ satisfy
$$\operatorname{ev}^B_{ST}\circ(h_T\otimes1_{ST})=u\circ S(\operatorname{ev}^A_T),$$
under the canonical tensor identifications. Then the following equality holds in $D(B)$, with common source $SK$ and target $D_B(SD_AK)$:
$$h_{D_AK}\circ S(\delta^A_K)=D_B(h_K)\circ\delta^B_{SK}.$$
If $h_K$ and $h_{D_AK}$ are isomorphisms, the identification
$$S(D_A^2K)\xrightarrow{h_{D_AK}}D_B(SD_AK)\xrightarrow{D_B(h_K)^{-1}}D_B^2(SK)$$
carries $S(\delta^A_K)$ to $\delta^B_{SK}$. The equality uses the same signed tensor symmetry on both sides: on homogeneous representatives of degrees $i,j$ scalar extension preserves the sign $(-1)^{ij}$. No constructibility, biduality-isomorphism, or flatness hypothesis on $B/A$ is required.

proof.text: Use the given CoefficientClosedStructure adjunctions and their evaluation_naturality fields [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. Identify each specified braiding on K-flat pairs with the native Koszul braiding: the symmetry_model field of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] supplies its pure-section formula, [lem-sf-ringed-tensor-complex-constraints] supplies the same formula for the native map, and the tensor-sheafification adjunction and total-degree coproduct universal property give equality. Apply the signed cochain scalar-comparison equation of [lem-pur-cochain-comparison-monoidal-equations]. The two TensorComparisonModel normalizations and naturality of the counit identify its localization with the desired symmetry square on K-flat pairs. Cancel their invertible counits, supplied by the given change-of-rings model [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Every derived object has a K-flat representative by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; naturality of the specified comparison and both braidings transports the square to all objects. No general ringed-topos comparison system is needed.

proof.text: For clarity retain all tensor comparisons. Set $V=D_AK$, $X=SK$, $Y=SV$, $h=h_K:Y\to D_BX$ and $h'=h_V:S(D_AV)\to D_BY$. Put $a=h'\circ S(\delta^A_K)$ and $b=D_B(h)\circ\delta^B_X$, both maps $X\to D_BY$. By the bijection in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], it suffices to compare $\mathcal U(f)=\operatorname{ev}^B_Y\circ(f\otimes1_Y):X\otimes_B^LY\to\Omega_B$ for $f=a,b$. This reduction uses injectivity of the bijection, without any invertibility of either $h$ or a double-dual map.

source.place: Sentence 'transposing evaluation as in lem-weil-duality-pairing gives double-dual compatibility', expanded by the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
Naturality of the tensor comparison, the assumed evaluation identity for $T=V$, and the defining transpose equation for $\delta^A_K$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal U(a)&=\operatorname{ev}^B_Y\circ(h'\otimes1_Y)\circ(S\delta^A_K\otimes1_Y)\\
&=u\circ S(\operatorname{ev}^A_V)\circ t_{D_AV,V}^{-1}\circ(S\delta^A_K\otimes1_Y)\\
&=u\circ S\bigl(\operatorname{ev}^A_V\circ(\delta^A_K\otimes1_V)\bigr)\circ t_{K,V}^{-1}\\
&=u\circ S\bigl(\operatorname{ev}^A_K\circ\tau^A_{K,V}\bigr)\circ t_{K,V}^{-1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is exactly the inverse-transpose formula of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], applied to the definition of $\delta^A_K$.

source.place: Sentence 'transposing evaluation as in lem-weil-duality-pairing gives double-dual compatibility', expanded by the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
The naturality in the tensor parameter of the adjunction in [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] says, for $h:Y\to D_BX$,
$$\operatorname{ev}^B_Y\circ(D_B(h)\otimes1_Y)=\operatorname{ev}^B_{D_BX}\circ(1_{D_B^2X}\otimes h).$$
Indeed, both maps are the inverse transpose of the precomposition map $H_B(h,\Omega_B)$: naturality in the parameter identifies precomposition of an uncurried map by $1\otimes h$ with postcomposition of its transpose by $H_B(h,\Omega_B)$. Tensor bifunctoriality and the transpose definition of $\delta^B_X$ now give
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal U(b)&=\operatorname{ev}^B_{D_BX}\circ(\delta^B_X\otimes1_{D_BX})\circ(1_X\otimes h)\\
&=\operatorname{ev}^B_X\circ\tau^B_{X,D_BX}\circ(1_X\otimes h)\\
&=\operatorname{ev}^B_X\circ(h\otimes1_X)\circ\tau^B_{X,Y}\\
&=u\circ S(\operatorname{ev}^A_K)\circ t_{V,K}^{-1}\circ\tau^B_{X,Y}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third equality is naturality of symmetry, and the last is the assumed evaluation identity for $T=K$.

source.place: Sentence 'transposing evaluation as in lem-weil-duality-pairing gives double-dual compatibility', expanded by the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text:
The scalar symmetry square proved in Step 1 is
$$t_{V,K}\circ S(\tau^A_{K,V})=\tau^B_{X,Y}\circ t_{K,V}.$$
Multiplying by the inverses of the two $t$'s gives $t_{V,K}^{-1}\circ\tau^B_{X,Y}=S(\tau^A_{K,V})\circ t_{K,V}^{-1}$. Substituting this in Step 4 makes its final expression exactly the last expression of Step 3. Thus $\mathcal U(a)=\mathcal U(b)$ and the injective transpose bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] gives $a=b$, the asserted equality. The cited symmetry is the one induced by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$ in bidegree $(i,j)$; scalar extension is additive and does not change degrees, so the comparison preserves that same factor $(-1)^{ij}$, also in characteristic two.

source.place: Sentence 'transposing evaluation as in lem-weil-duality-pairing gives double-dual compatibility', expanded by the tensor-Hom adjunction

proof.text: Suppose now that $h$ and $h'$ are isomorphisms. The contravariant functor $D_B=H_B(-,\Omega_B)$ sends the inverse of $h$ to the inverse of $D_B(h)$: applying the functor to $h^{-1}h=1$ and $hh^{-1}=1$ verifies both inverse identities. Postcompose the equality $h'\circ S(\delta^A_K)=D_B(h)\circ\delta^B_X$ with $D_B(h)^{-1}$. Cancellation yields $D_B(h)^{-1}\circ h'\circ S(\delta^A_K)=\delta^B_X$, precisely the requested identification. No assertion that either $\delta$ is invertible was used.
